summary.short: Implements EU Directive 2016/1148 (NIS) in the UK from 10 May 2018: sets security and incident-notification duties for operators of essential services and relevant digital service providers, with designated authorities and penalties up to £17,000,000.
summary.long: Implements Directive (EU) 2016/1148 (the NIS Directive) in the UK, in force 10 May 2018. Requires a national NIS strategy and designates sector competent authorities; GCHQ is the single point of contact and CSIRT (regs 2–5). Persons providing essential services above Schedule 2 thresholds are deemed operators of essential services (OES), or may be designated by a competent authority (reg. 8). OES must take appropriate security measures and notify significant incidents within 72 hours (regs 10–11). Relevant digital service providers (online marketplaces, online search engines, cloud computing services), other than micro or small enterprises, must manage security risks, notify substantial incidents within 72 hours and register with the Information Commission (regs 12–14). Non-UK providers offering digital services in the UK must nominate a UK representative (reg. 14A). Enforcement tools include information notices, inspections, enforcement notices and penalty notices (regs 15–18). Penalties are capped at £1,000,000 for non-material contraventions and £8,500,000 or £17,000,000 for material ones. Appeals lie to the First-tier Tribunal (regs 19A–19B); penalties are recoverable as court orders (reg. 20). Fees and periodic review reports are also covered (regs 21, 25).

notes: Text shows amendment markers (F-numbers) and omitted provisions as dotted lines; amendments are not coded as relations because the text does not name the amending acts. Target instrument IDs are not in the registry and are left empty. Inconsistencies: regulation 25(2) requires review reports at intervals not exceeding five years, while the Explanatory Note says reviews must be biennial; regulation 18(2) refers to 'the duty set out in regulation (3A)' without the number 17; the Explanatory Note names the regulator the Information Commissioner while the Regulations use Information Commission; the Explanatory Note says regulation 19 provides independent review, but regulation 19 is headed only and the appeal provisions sit in regulations 19A and 19B. Entities list competent authorities only; OES and RDSP addressees are roles, not named entities. Lei and ticker are not verifiable from the text.

“digital service” means a service within the meaning of point (b) of Article 1(1) of Directive 2015/1535 which is of any the following kinds
“digital service provider” means any person who provides a digital service
“online marketplace” means a digital service that allows consumers and/or traders
“online search engine” means a digital service that allows users to perform searches of, in principle, all websites
“cloud computing service” means a digital service that enables access to a scalable and elastic pool of shareable computing resources
“essential service” means a service which is essential for the maintenance of critical societal or economic activities
“network and information system” (“NIS”) means—
“OES” (“operator of an essential service”) means a person who is deemed to be designated as an operator of an essential service under regulation 8(1)
a “relevant digital service provider” (“RDSP”) is a reference to a person who provides a digital service in the United Kingdom
“incident” means any event having an actual adverse effect on the security of network and information systems

definitions.term: security of network and information systems

evidence.quote: “security of network and information systems” means the ability of network and information systems to resist
“representative” means any natural or legal person established in the United Kingdom who is able to act on behalf of a digital service provider established outside the United Kingdom
“oil equivalent” means petroleum and, for the purposes of assessments of throughput, where petroleum is in a gaseous state 1,100 cubic meters
“affiliated undertaking” has the meaning given by Article 2(12) of Directive 2013/34/EU
“final customer” has the meaning given by Article 2(9) of the Electricity Directive
“road authority” has the same meaning
“TLD Name Registry” is a reference to “top-level domain name registry” which means an entity which administers and operates the registration of internet domain names under a specific top-level domain
which means an entity which provides DNS services
“IXP” is a reference to “internet exchange point” which means a network facility which
“IXP Operator” means a person who provides an IXP to another person

enforcement.max_penalty_text: Not exceed £1,000,000 for a non-material contravention; not exceed £8,500,000 for a material contravention not meeting the significant-risk criteria; not exceed £17,000,000 for a material contravention that has or could have created a significant risk to, or significant impact on, the service provision
enforcement.penalty_formula: Tiered caps: £1,000,000 for any non-material contravention; £8,500,000 for a material contravention; £17,000,000 for a material contravention that has or could have created a significant risk to, or significant impact on, the service provision. Amount must be appropriate and proportionate to the failure.
